Definition: to sink or depress (reflexive or causative)
BiblicalUsage: Shachach is to sink down, and the psalms use it for the soul itself, cast down and disquieted within. Three times the psalmist asks his own soul why it is cast down, and each time answers with hope in God. Isaiah lifts the same word to the nations, where the lofty looks of man shall be humbled and the haughtiness of men bowed down, and the LORD alone exalted.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a cast-down soul is not a faithless soul, because the psalmist preaches hope to himself while he is still down. God does not leave His people bowed, and He will not leave the proud standing either. That is why I answer my own heaviness the way the psalmist did, with hope in God.
